questions.q: Choose the correct representation of conductometric titration of benzoic acid vs sodium hydroxide.
questions.solution:
${C}_{6}{H}_{5}\mathop{C}_{\left(WA\right)}OOH + Na\mathop{O}_{\left(SB\right)}H \to {C}_{6}{H}_{5}\mathop{C}_{\left(Salt\right)}OONa + {H}_{2}O$

 Initially the conductance is low due to the feeble ionisation of acetic acid. On the addition of base, there is decrease in conductance($A \to B$) not only due to the replacement of${H}^{+}$ by ${Na}^{+}$ but also suppresses the dissociation of benzoic acid due to common ion benzoate. But very soon, the conductance increases($B \to C$) on adding $NaOH$ as $NaOH$ neutralises the un-dissociated ${C}_{6}{H}_{5}COOH$ to ${C}_{6}{H}_{5}COONa$ which is the strong electrolyte. This increase in conductance continues raise up to the equivalence point. The graph near the equivalence point is curved due the hydrolysis of salt ${C}_{6}{H}_{5}COONa$. Beyond the equivalence point, conductance increases($C \to D$) more rapidly with the addition of $NaOH$ due to the highly conducting ${OH}^{-}$ ions

questions.q:
Given below are two statements: One is labelled as Assertion $A$ and the other is labelled as Reason $R$

Assertion $A$ : Permanganate titration are not performed in presence of hydrochloric acid.

Reason $R$ : Chlorine is formed as a consequence of oxidation of hydrochloric acid.

In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below
options: Both $A$ and $R$ are true and $R$ is the correct explanation of $A$
Both $A$ and $R$ are true but $R$ is NOT the correct explanation of $A$
questions.solution:
Hydrochloric acid (HCl) is usually not used in the process of titration because it reacts with the indicator potassium permanganate $( {KMnO}_{4} )$ that is used in the process. It reacts with ${KMnO}_{4}$ solution and gets oxidized which further results in the liberation of chlorine gas according to the following reaction.

$2{KMnO}_{4} + 16HCl \to 2{MnCl}_{2} + 2KCl + 8{H}_{2}O + 5{Cl}_{2}$

So, Both $A$ and $R$ are true and $R$ is the correct explanation of $A$

Assertion :- The average oxidation no. of sulphur in \(\mathrm{Na}_2 \mathrm{~S}_4 \mathrm{O}_6\) is 2.5

options: Both (A) and (R) are correct but (R) is not the correct explanation of (A).
(A) is correct but (R) is not correct.
(A) is not correct but (R) is correct.
Both (A) and (R) are correct and (R) is the correct explanation of (A).
questions.solution:
- Assertion (A): Correct. In \(\mathrm{Na}_2 \mathrm{~S}_4 \mathrm{O}_6\) (tetrathionate ion), the average oxidation state of sulfur is indeed +2.5.
- Reason (R): Incorrect. The fact that two sulfur atoms are not directly linked with oxygen atoms is unrelated to the calculation of the average oxidation state. The average oxidation number is determined by the overall structure and oxidation states of individual sulfur atoms, not by their direct linkage to oxygen.
Thus, (A) is correct but (R) is not correct.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q:
The exhibition of various oxidation states by an element is also related to the outer orbital electronic configuration of its atom. Atom (s) having which of the following outermost electronic configurations will exhibit more than one oxidation state in its compounds.
(a) \(3 \mathrm{~s}^{\prime}\)
(b) \(3 d^{\prime} 4 s^2\)
(c) \(3 d^2 4 s^2\)
(d) \(3 s^2 3 p^3\)
questions.solution:
Elements which have only s-electrons in the valence shell do not show more than one oxidation state. Thus, element with \(3 s^1\) as outer electronic configuration shows only one oxidation state of +1.
Transition element such as elements (b), (c) having incompletely filled \(d\)-orbitals in the penultimate shell show variable oxidation states. Thus, element with outer electronic configuration as \(3 d^1 4 s^2\) shows variable oxidation states of +2 and +3 and the element with outer electronic configuration as \(3 d^2 4 s^2\) shows variable oxidation states of \(+2,+3\) and +4.
p-Block elements also show variable oxidation states due to a number of reason such as involvement of \(d\)-orbitals and inert pair effect e.g., element (d) with \(3 s^2 3 p^3\) as (i.e., P) as the outer electronic configuration shows variable oxidation states of +3 and +5 due to involvement of \(d\)-orbitals.

questions.q:
Match the following:
The correct answer is
questions.solution:
(A) $\mathrm{TiCl}_4(l)+2 \mathrm{Mg}(s) \stackrel{\Delta}{\longrightarrow} \mathrm{Ti}(s)+2 \mathrm{MgCl}_2(s)$
The above reaction is an example of metal displacement reaction in which more reactive metal. (i.e. $\mathrm{Mg}$ ) will displace less reactive metal (i.e. Ti).
Thus, option (II) is related with (A).
(B) $2 \mathrm{H}_2 \mathrm{O}_2(a q) \longrightarrow 2 \mathrm{H}_2 \mathrm{O}(l)+\mathrm{O}_2(g)$
The above reaction is an example of disproportionation reaction in which $\mathrm{O}$-atom of $\mathrm{H}_2 \mathrm{O}_2$ is oxidised as $\left(\mathrm{O}_2\right)$ and also reduced to $\mathrm{H}_2 \mathrm{O}$. Thus, option (I) is related with (B).
(C) $\mathrm{C}(s)+\mathrm{O}_2(g) \stackrel{\Delta}{\longrightarrow} \mathrm{CO}_2(g)$
The above reaction is an example of combination reaction in which carbon(s) combines with $\mathrm{O}_2(g)$ to give $\mathrm{CO}_2(g)$. Thus, option (IV) is related with (C).
(D) $2 \mathrm{NaH}(s) \stackrel{\Delta}{\longrightarrow} 2 \mathrm{Na}(s)+\mathrm{H}_2(g)$
The above reaction is an example of decomposition reaction in which $\mathrm{NaH}$ is decomposes to $\mathrm{Na}(s) and \mathrm{H}_2(g)$. Thus, option (III) is related with (D).
Hence,
$(\mathrm{A}) \rightarrow(\mathrm{II}),(\mathrm{B}) \rightarrow(\mathrm{I}),(\mathrm{C}) \rightarrow(\mathrm{IV}),(\mathrm{D}) \rightarrow(\mathrm{III})$
and option (a) is the correct answer.

questions.q:
Given below are two statements: one is labelled as Assertion (A) and the other is labelled as Reason (R).

Assertion (A): The average oxidation state of bromine in $\text{Br}_3\text{O}_8$ is $+\dfrac{16}{3}$, but the individual oxidation states of the bromine atoms are $+6$, $+4$, and $+6$.
Reason (R): In the linear structure of $\text{Br}_3\text{O}_8$, the terminal bromine atoms are bonded to three oxygen atoms each, while the central bromine atom is bonded to two oxygen atoms.

In the light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below:
options: Both (A) and (R) are correct but (R) is not the correct explanation of (A)
Both (A) and (R) are correct and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)
(A) is correct but (R) is not correct
(A) is not correct but (R) is correct
questions.solution:
The chemical formula of tribromooctaoxide is $\text{Br}_3\text{O}_8$.

Let the average oxidation state of Br be $x$.
$3x + 8(-2) = 0 \Rightarrow x = +\dfrac{16}{3}$

The structure of $\text{Br}_3\text{O}_8$ is $\text{O}_3\text{Br}-\text{BrO}_2-\text{BrO}_3$.
The terminal bromine atoms are each bonded to three oxygen atoms (which are more electronegative), so their oxidation state is $+6$.
The central bromine atom is bonded to two oxygen atoms, so its oxidation state is $+4$.

Thus, the individual oxidation states are $+6$, $+4$, and $+6$. The structural arrangement correctly explains the individual and average oxidation states.

Therefore, both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are correct and (R) is the correct explanation of (A).

Answer: Both (A) and (R) are correct and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)

questions.q: Identify the correct increasing order of the oxidation state of nitrogen in the following species.
questions.solution:
Let us calculate the oxidation state of nitrogen ($x$) in each species.

In $\text{NH}_4^+$: $x + 4(+1) = +1 \Rightarrow x = -3$

In $\text{N}_2\text{H}_4$: $2x + 4(+1) = 0 \Rightarrow 2x = -4 \Rightarrow x = -2$

In $\text{NO}_2^-$: $x + 2(-2) = -1 \Rightarrow x - 4 = -1 \Rightarrow x = +3$

In $\text{NO}_3^-$: $x + 3(-2) = -1 \Rightarrow x - 6 = -1 \Rightarrow x = +5$

The increasing order of oxidation states is $-3 < -2 < +3 < +5$.

Hence, the correct sequence is $\text{NH}_4^+ < \text{N}_2\text{H}_4 < \text{NO}_2^- < \text{NO}_3^-$.

Answer: $\text{NH}_4^+ < \text{N}_2\text{H}_4 < \text{NO}_2^- < \text{NO}_3^-$

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: The oxidation states of the central atoms in $\text{CrO}_5$ and $\text{H}_2\text{SO}_5$ are respectively:
questions.solution:
By standard rules, the oxidation state of Cr in $\text{CrO}_5$ would be $+10$ ($x - 10 = 0$) and S in $\text{H}_2\text{SO}_5$ would be $+8$ ($2 + x - 10 = 0$). However, these exceed the maximum possible oxidation states for Cr (Group 6) and S (Group 16), which are both $+6$.

This discrepancy is due to the presence of peroxy linkages in their structures.

In $\text{CrO}_5$ (butterfly structure), there are two peroxy linkages (four oxygen atoms with $-1$ oxidation state) and one oxide linkage (one oxygen atom with $-2$ oxidation state).
$x + 4(-1) + 1(-2) = 0 \Rightarrow x = +6$

In $\text{H}_2\text{SO}_5$ (Caro's acid), there is one peroxy linkage (two oxygen atoms with $-1$ oxidation state) and three normal oxygen atoms ($-2$ oxidation state).
$2(+1) + x + 3(-2) + 2(-1) = 0 \Rightarrow x = +6$

Thus, the oxidation states of Cr and S are $+6$ and $+6$ respectively.

Answer: $+6$ and $+6$

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Some compounds contain atoms of the same element in different oxidation states. In which of the following compounds is the mathematical difference between the highest and lowest oxidation states of the same element maximum?
questions.solution:
To find the maximum difference, we must determine the individual oxidation states of the atoms of the same element in each mixed compound.

For $\text{CaOCl}_2$ (bleaching powder): It consists of $\text{Ca}^{2+}$, $\text{Cl}^-$ and $\text{OCl}^-$ ions. The oxidation states of chlorine are $-1$ and $+1$. The difference is $|+1 - (-1)| = 2$.

For $\text{NH}_4\text{NO}_3$: It consists of $\text{NH}_4^+$ and $\text{NO}_3^-$ ions. Let the oxidation state of N in $\text{NH}_4^+$ be $x$: $x + 4(+1) = +1 \Rightarrow x = -3$. Let the oxidation state of N in $\text{NO}_3^-$ be $y$: $y + 3(-2) = -1 \Rightarrow y = +5$. The difference is $|+5 - (-3)| = 8$.

For $\text{Pb}_3\text{O}_4$: It is a mixed oxide of $2\text{PbO} \cdot \text{PbO}_2$. The oxidation states of lead are $+2$ and $+4$. The difference is $|+4 - (+2)| = 2$.

For $\text{Fe}_3\text{O}_4$: It is a mixed oxide of $\text{FeO} \cdot \text{Fe}_2\text{O}_3$. The oxidation states of iron are $+2$ and $+3$. The difference is $|+3 - (+2)| = 1$.

The maximum difference is $8$, found in $\text{NH}_4\text{NO}_3$.

Answer: $\text{NH}_4\text{NO}_3$

questions.q: Which of the following species cannot act as both an oxidizing and a reducing agent?
questions.solution:
For a species to act as both an oxidizing and a reducing agent, the element undergoing the redox change must be in an intermediate oxidation state.

Let us calculate the oxidation state of the key element in each species:
1) In $\text{H}_2\text{O}_2$, the oxidation state of oxygen is $-1$. It can be oxidized to $0$ (in $\text{O}_2$) or reduced to $-2$ (in $\text{H}_2\text{O}$).
2) In $\text{SO}_2$, the oxidation state of sulphur is $+4$. It can be oxidized to $+6$ or reduced to lower states.
3) In $\text{HNO}_3$, the oxidation state of nitrogen is $+5$. This is the maximum possible oxidation state for nitrogen (Group 15). Therefore, it cannot be oxidized further and can only act as an oxidizing agent.
4) In $\text{HNO}_2$, the oxidation state of nitrogen is $+3$, which is an intermediate state.

Thus, $\text{HNO}_3$ cannot act as both an oxidizing and a reducing agent.

Answer: $\text{HNO}_3$

questions.q:
White phosphorus reacts with aqueous alkali as shown in the following equation:

$\text{P}_4 + 3\text{OH}^- + 3\text{H}_2\text{O} \rightarrow \text{PH}_3 + 3\text{H}_2\text{PO}_2^-$

What are the changes in the oxidation number of phosphorus in this disproportionation reaction?
questions.solution:
In elemental white phosphorus ($\text{P}_4$), the oxidation number of phosphorus is $0$.

In phosphine ($\text{PH}_3$), let the oxidation number of P be $x$.
The oxidation number of H is $+1$.
$x + 3(+1) = 0$
$x = -3$

In the hypophosphite ion ($\text{H}_2\text{PO}_2^-$), let the oxidation number of P be $y$.
The oxidation number of H is $+1$ and O is $-2$.
$y + 2(+1) + 2(-2) = -1$
$y + 2 - 4 = -1$
$y - 2 = -1$
$y = +1$

Thus, the oxidation number of phosphorus changes from $0$ to $-3$ and from $0$ to $+1$.

Answer: $0$ to $-3$ and $0$ to $+1$

The central bromine atom is bonded to two oxygen atoms via double bonds (and to two bromine atoms, which do not contribute to the oxidation state difference). Therefore, the oxidation state of the central bromine atom is +4.

The average oxidation state is $+\dfrac{16}{3}$, but the individual oxidation states of the terminal and central bromine atoms are +6 and +4, respectively.

Answer: +6 and +4

questions.q:
Given below are two statements: one is labelled as Assertion (A) and the other is labelled as Reason (R).

Assertion (A): In the conversion of dichromate ion ($\text{Cr}_2\text{O}_7^{2-}$) to $\text{Cr}^{3+}$, the oxidation state of chromium changes from $+6$ to $+3$.

Reason (R): The oxidation state of oxygen is $-2$ in all of its compounds.

In the light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below:
options: Both (A) and (R) are true and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)
Both (A) and (R) are true but (R) is not the correct explanation of (A)
questions.solution:
Assertion (A) is true: Let the oxidation state of Cr in $\text{Cr}_2\text{O}_7^{2-}$ be $x$.
$2x + 7(-2) = -2$
$2x - 14 = -2$
$2x = +12$
$x = +6$
The oxidation state of Cr changes from $+6$ in $\text{Cr}_2\text{O}_7^{2-}$ to $+3$ in $\text{Cr}^{3+}$.

Reason (R) is false: The oxidation state of oxygen is $-2$ in most of its compounds, but there are exceptions. For example, in peroxides (like $\text{H}_2\text{O}_2$) it is $-1$, in superoxides (like $\text{KO}_2$) it is $-1/2$, and in oxygen fluorides (like $\text{OF}_2$) it is $+2$.

Thus, (A) is true but (R) is false.

Answer: (A) is true but (R) is false

questions.q:
Identify the correct increasing order of the actual oxidation state of the underlined atom in the following species:
$\underline{\text{O}}\text{F}_2$, $\underline{\text{Pb}}\text{O}_2$, $\underline{\text{Cr}}\text{O}_5$, $\text{K}\underline{\text{Mn}}\text{O}_4$
questions.solution:
Let us calculate the actual oxidation state of the underlined atom in each compound.

In $\text{OF}_2$: Fluorine is more electronegative than oxygen and always has an oxidation state of $-1$. Let the oxidation state of O be $x$.
$x + 2(-1) = 0 \Rightarrow x = +2$.

In $\text{PbO}_2$: It is a normal oxide (lead dioxide), not a peroxide. Let the oxidation state of Pb be $y$.
$y + 2(-2) = 0 \Rightarrow y = +4$.

In $\text{CrO}_5$: Calculating algebraically gives $z + 5(-2) = 0 \Rightarrow z = +10$, which is impossible since chromium belongs to group 6 and its maximum oxidation state is $+6$. Structurally, $\text{CrO}_5$ has a butterfly structure with one double-bonded oxygen ($-2$) and four oxygen atoms in two peroxide linkages ($-1$ each).
Actual oxidation state of Cr $= +6$.

In $\text{KMnO}_4$: Let the oxidation state of Mn be $w$.
$+1 + w + 4(-2) = 0 \Rightarrow w = +7$.

The actual oxidation states are $+2$ (O), $+4$ (Pb), $+6$ (Cr), and $+7$ (Mn).
The correct increasing order is: $\text{OF}_2 < \text{PbO}_2 < \text{CrO}_5 < \text{KMnO}_4$.

Options assuming Cr is $+10$ or Pb is $+2$ (by wrongly assuming $\text{PbO}_2$ is a peroxide) are incorrect.

Answer: $\underline{\text{O}}\text{F}_2 < \underline{\text{Pb}}\text{O}_2 < \underline{\text{Cr}}\text{O}_5 < \text{K}\underline{\text{Mn}}\text{O}_4$

questions.q:
Given below are two statements: one is labelled as Assertion (A) and the other is labelled as Reason (R).

Assertion (A): The oxidation state of sulphur in $\mathrm{H_2S_2O_8}$ (Marshall's acid) is +6.
Reason (R): $\mathrm{H_2S_2O_8}$ contains one peroxide linkage ($-\mathrm{O}-\mathrm{O}-$) in its structure.

In the light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below:
options: Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are correct but Reason (R) is not the correct explanation for Assertion (A)
Assertion (A) is correct but Reason (R) is incorrect
Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are correct and Reason (R) is the correct explanation for Assertion (A)
Assertion (A) is incorrect but Reason (R) is correct
questions.solution:
Assertion (A) is correct: The maximum oxidation state of sulphur (Group 16) cannot exceed +6. In $\mathrm{H_2S_2O_8}$, the oxidation state of sulphur is indeed +6.

Reason (R) is correct and explains Assertion (A): If the oxidation state of sulphur is calculated algebraically assuming all oxygen atoms are in the -2 oxidation state, the result is $2x + 8(-2) = 0 \Rightarrow x = +8$, which is impossible. The structure of Marshall's acid is $\mathrm{HO-SO_2-O-O-SO_2-OH}$. It contains one peroxide linkage ($-\mathrm{O}-\mathrm{O}-$) where two oxygen atoms have an oxidation state of -1.

Calculating correctly: $2x + 6(-2) + 2(-1) = 0 \Rightarrow 2x - 14 = 0 \Rightarrow x = +6$. Thus, the presence of the peroxide linkage explains why the oxidation state is +6 rather than the algebraically calculated +8.

Answer: Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are correct and Reason (R) is the correct explanation for Assertion (A)

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: What is the oxidation state of sulphur in Caro's acid ($\mathrm{H_2SO_5}$)?
questions.solution:
By a conventional algebraic calculation, the oxidation state of $\mathrm{S}$ in $\mathrm{H_2SO_5}$ would appear to be:
$2(+1) + x + 5(-2) = 0 \Rightarrow x = +8$

However, sulphur belongs to Group 16 and has a maximum possible oxidation state of +6. The anomaly arises because the structure of Caro's acid (peroxomonosulfuric acid) contains one peroxide linkage ($\mathrm{-O-O-}$).

Thus, it has three oxygen atoms with a normal oxidation state of -2, and two oxygen atoms in the peroxide linkage with an oxidation state of -1.
The correct calculation is:
$2(+1) + x + 3(-2) + 2(-1) = 0$
$2 + x - 6 - 2 = 0 \Rightarrow x = +6$

The incorrect options stem from ignoring the peroxide linkage (+8), making arithmetic errors (+4), or incorrectly assuming multiple peroxide linkages (+5).

Answer: +6

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: In an acidic medium, $10$ mL of $0.25$ M oxalic acid is titrated with KMnO$_4$ solution. If the volume of KMnO$_4$ solution required to reach end point is $10$ mL, the strength of the KMnO$_4$ solution is
questions.solution:
In an acidic medium, the reaction of KMnO$_4$ with oxalic acid involves the following changes in oxidation states:

For KMnO$_4$, Mn$^{7+} \rightarrow$ Mn$^{2+}$, so the n-factor is $5$.

For oxalic acid (H$_2$C$_2$O$_4$), C$^{3+} \rightarrow$ C$^{4+}$, so the n-factor is $2 \times 1 = 2$.

At the equivalence point, the number of equivalents of KMnO$_4$ equals the number of equivalents of oxalic acid:

$N_1 V_1 = N_2 V_2$

$(M_1 \times n_1) V_1 = (M_2 \times n_2) V_2$

Substituting the given values:

$M_1 \times 5 \times 10 = 0.25 \times 2 \times 10$

$50 M_1 = 5$

$M_1 = 0.10$ M

The strength of the KMnO$_4$ solution is $0.10$ M.

questions.q:
Which of the following reactions are disproportionation reaction?

$\left(a\right) 2C{u}^{+} \to C{u}^{2 +} + C{u}^{0}$

$\left(b\right) 3Mn{O}_{4}^{2 -} + 4{H}^{+} \to 2Mn{O}_{4}^{-} + Mn{O}_{2} + 2{H}_{2}O$

$\left(c\right) 2KMn{O}_{4}\overset{∆}{\to}{K}_{2}Mn{O}_{4} + Mn{O}_{2} + {O}_{2}$

$\left(d\right) 2Mn{O}_{4}^{-} + 3M{n}^{2 +} + 2{H}_{2}O \to 5Mn{O}_{2} + 4{H}^{⊕}$

Select the correct option from the following:
questions.solution:
The redox reactions in which the same species is getting oxidised (increase in oxidation number) and reduced (decrease in oxidation number).

(i) $\overset{( + 1 )}{2C{u}^{+}} \to \overset{( + 2 )}{C{u}^{+ 2}} + \overset{( 0 )}{C{u}^{0}} \to$ Disproportionation

(ii) $\overset{( + 6 )}{3Mn{O}_{4}^{2 -}} + 4{H}^{+} \to \overset{( + 7 )}{2Mn{O}_{4}^{-}} + \overset{( + 4 )}{Mn{O}_{2}} + 2{H}_{2}O \to$ Disproportionation

(iii) $\overset{\left(+ 7\right)}{2KMn{O}_{4}}\overset{\Delta}{\to}\overset{\left(+ 6\right)}{{K}_{2}Mn{O}_{4}} + \overset{\left(+ 4\right)}{Mn{O}_{2}} + {O}_{2}$

Only reduction is happening here.

(iv) $\overset{\left(+ 7\right)}{2Mn{O}_{4}^{-}} + \overset{\left(+ 2\right)}{3M{n}^{+ 2}} \to \overset{\left(+ 4\right)}{5Mn{O}_{2}}$

Different species are getting oxidised and reduced. Hence, the correct options are (i) and (ii) only.

questions.q: In which of the following compounds, nitrogen exhibits highest oxidation state?
questions.solution:
Let the oxidation state of nitrogen in the given compounds be \(x\).
(a) \(\mathrm{N}_2 \mathrm{H}_4\)
$\begin{aligned}
& 2(x)+(+1) 4=0 \\
& 2 x=-4
\end{aligned}\)
So, \(x=-2\).
(b) \(\mathrm{NH}_3\)
\(x+(+1)^3=0\)
So, \(x=-3\)
(c) \(\mathrm{N}_3 \mathrm{H}\)
\begin{aligned}
& (x) 3+(+1)=0 \\
& 3 x=-1
\end{aligned}$
So, \(x=-1 / 3\)
(d) \(\mathrm{NH}_2 \mathrm{OH}\)
$\begin{aligned}
& x+(+1) 2+(-2)+(+1)=0 \\
& x+2-2+1=0 \\
& x+1=0
\end{aligned}$
So, \(x=-1\)
Thus, oxidation state of nitrogen is highest in \(\mathrm{N}_3 \mathrm{H}\).

In the given reaction, the oxidation number of bromine increases from 0 to +1 and decreases from 0 to -1 .

: \mathrm{H}_2 \mathrm{O}+\stackrel{0}{\mathrm{Br}_2} \longrightarrow \mathrm{HOBr}+\mathrm{HBr}^{-1}
$$

Some students understood that the given reaction is redox reaction, but confuse with fact that redox reaction is the reaction in both oxidation and reduction occurs.

questions.q:
Assertion: The correct order of oxidising power is : $\mathrm{VO}_2^{+} < \mathrm{Cr}_2 \mathrm{O}_7^{2-} < \mathrm{MnO}_4^{-}$
Reason: The oxidation state of $\mathrm{Mn}$ is +7 .
options: If both assertion and reason are true and reason is the correct explanation of assertion.
If both assertion and reason are true but reason is not the correct explanation of assertion.
If assertion is true but reason is false.
If both assertion and reason are false.
questions.solution:
The oxidation states of the given compounds are
$\begin{aligned} & \mathrm{VO}_2^{+}: x+2(-2)=+1 \\ & \Rightarrow x=+5 \\ & \mathrm{Cr}_2 \mathrm{O}_7^{2-}: 2 x+7(-2)=-2 \\ & \Rightarrow 2 x=+12 \\ & \Rightarrow x=+6 \\ & \mathrm{MnO}_4^{-}: x+4(-2)=-1 \\ & \quad x=-1+8=+7\end{aligned}$
The correct order of oxidising power is $\mathrm{VO}_2^{+} < \mathrm{Cr}_2 \mathrm{O}_7^{2-} < \mathrm{MnO}_4^{-}$
due to the increasing stability of the lower species to which they are reduced.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Which of the following is disproportionation reaction?
questions.solution:
Reactions in which the same substance is oxidised as well as reduced are called disproportionation reaction. Writing the oxidation number of each element above its symbol in the given reactions.
$\begin{aligned} & \stackrel{-4}{\mathrm{C}} \stackrel{+1}{h}_4+4 \mathrm{Cl}_2^{\circ} \longrightarrow \stackrel{+4}{\mathrm{C}} \mathrm{Cl}_4+4 \stackrel{+1-1}{\mathrm{HCl}} \\ & 2 \mathrm{~F}_2^0+2 \stackrel{-2}{\mathrm{O}} \mathrm{H}^{-} \longrightarrow 2 \stackrel{-1}{\mathrm{~F}}+\stackrel{+2}{\mathrm{O}} \mathrm{F}_2^{-1}+\stackrel{-1}{\mathrm{H}_2 \mathrm{O}_{\mathrm{O}}^{-2} \\ & 2 \stackrel{+4-2}{\mathrm{~N} \mathrm{O}_2}+2 \mathrm{OH}^{-2} \longrightarrow \stackrel{+3}{\mathrm{NO}_2^{-2}}+\stackrel{+5}{\mathrm{NO}_3^{-2}}+\stackrel{+1}{\mathrm{H}_2} \mathrm{O}^{-2} \\ & \end{aligned}$
Thus, in the reaction of $\mathrm{NO}_2 and \mathrm{OH}^{-}, \mathrm{N}$ is both oxidised as well as reduced. Hence, the oxidation number increases from +4 in $\mathrm{NO}_2$ to +5 in $\mathrm{NO}_3^{-}$ and decreases from +4 in $\mathrm{NO}_2$ to +3 in $\mathrm{NO}_2^{-}$.

Thus, in the reaction of $\mathrm{NO}_2 and \mathrm{OH}^{-}, \mathrm{N}$ is both oxidised as well as reduced. Hence, the oxidation number increases from +4 in $\mathrm{NO}_2$ to +5 in $\mathrm{NO}_3^{-}$ and decreases from +4 in $\mathrm{NO}_2$ to +3 in $\mathrm{NO}_2^{-}$.

questions.q: The number of moles of $\mathrm{KMnO}_4$ reduced by one mole of KI in alkaline medium is
questions.solution: In alkaline solution, $\mathrm{KMnO}_4$ is reduced to $\mathrm{MnO}_2$ (colourless). Hence, two moles of $\mathrm{KMnO}_4$ are reduced by one mole of KI.
